title: Planning: LICHEN 2 PHY + regulatory roadmap
description:
Planning bead capturing the LICHEN 2 vision and regulatory path. NOT actionable implementation work — roadmap and decision tracking only.

## LICHEN 2 PHY Vision
Full 902-928 MHz band (26 MHz) with 500Hz or 250Hz chirps (LR-FHSS-style), per-frequency duty cycle limit + total band power budget. Enables ~50-100 simultaneous orthogonal transmissions, ~500-2000 nodes before congestion. SX1262 already supports LR-FHSS (488/244 Hz channels) for LoRaWAN uplink — LICHEN 2 extends to bidirectional mesh.

Everything above link layer survives from LICHEN 1 (IPv6, SCHC, RPL, OSCORE, CoAP, DTN, node classes). Changes: PHY (single-channel CSS → FHSS multi-channel), MAC (CSMA/TDMA → time-frequency grid), CCP becomes distributed spectrum coordination.

## Regulatory Path (FCC, 902-928 MHz)

### Phase 1: Development (no cost, immediate)
- Part 97 amateur radio: 1500W PEP, any modulation, no encryption (auth ok per recent ruling). Licensed hams only, no commercial use. Good for protocol dev and range testing.

### Phase 2: Demos (free, 2-4 weeks)
- FCC Experimental License (Part 5, Form 442): flexible power, specific areas/times. Conference demos and field R&D.

### Phase 3: Production (10-15K per device, 3-6 months)
- Part 15.247 FHSS device certification: 1W conducted + 6dBi antenna. LICHEN 2 FHSS params (≥50 hop channels, ≤400ms dwell) fit within existing rules by design.
- Pre-certified module firmware: work with Semtech/RAK/Heltec to certify LICHEN 2 firmware as part of module grant. Other products inherit certification.
- LICHEN Compliance Test Suite: like Wi-Fi Alliance — devices passing suite are Part 15.247 compliant by construction.

### Phase 4: Higher power (12-24 months, if needed)
- FCC waiver petition: argue that LICHEN 2 FHSS is demonstrably better-behaved (narrow chirps = less interference, strict per-freq duty cycle, provable aggregate power budget) to get higher EIRP than standard Part 15.247.

### Phase 5: Light licensing (years, LICHEN 3)
- CBRS-style approach: distributed spectrum coordination (CCP as distributed SAS). Requires FCC rulemaking/lobbying.

## Current State (LICHEN 1)
No new certification needed. T-Echo, RAK4631, etc. use SX1262 modules already FCC Part 15.247 certified. LICHEN 1 firmware operates within existing module grants (SF10, 125kHz, ≤1W).

## Key Decision Points
- Hardware path: SX1262 LR-FHSS mode (limited) vs SDR prototyping vs next-gen Semtech silicon
- Full BPv7 gateway interop also deferred to LICHEN 2
- When does 1W become insufficient? That triggers the waiver path.
